subject: Control-plane / Data-plane synthesis + handoff checkpoints for private VPC
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: netops@acme.com, edgeops@example.net
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Control-plane / Data-plane synthesis + handoff checkpoints for private VPC

Hi team — attaching the consolidated reference diagram and a lightweight handoff checklist for the upcoming ACME private VPC cutover. This consolidates the control-plane/data-plane split we discussed in last week's call and highlights the key checkpoints we need to validate during staging and the first 48h post-cutover.

High-level notes: 
- Control plane: customer-managed control-plane endpoints (API, provisioning) will live in the management VPC; data plane (runtime inference) lives in the tenant VPCs.
- Auth & certs: short-lived certs for control-plane to runtime comms (mutual TLS); KMS-backed keyring for signing AND SNI-based cert routing at the ingress edge.
- Egress policy: default-deny outbound for runtime nodes; explicit allowlist for telemetry endpoints (Redwood metrics, S3 endpoints).
- Fallback: a pre-approved fallback model variant hosted in region-us-east-1 (lower-capacity instance) that traffic will route to if tenant runtime reports > 95th pct CPU for 2 consecutive minutes or if the control-plane heartbeat fails for 30s.

Action items for ACME: please confirm the control-plane FQDNs in the topology_sketch_v3.png attachment and confirm ACLs for the egress allowlist. For Redwood: we will prepare the staging runbook diffs (runbook_deltas.txt) and complete the handoff_checklist_v2.xlsx before the preflight.

I’ve linked the Drive copy here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cACME-Topology (see Diagram v3).

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Infrastructure Manager, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Attachments:
- topology_sketch_v3.png (PNG, 1.2 MB) — consolidated control/data lanes
- handoff_checklist_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 120 KB) — staged checkpoints and owner column
- runbook_deltas.txt (TXT, 6 KB) — delta vs. default private-deploy runbook

From: netops@acme.com <netops@acme.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, edgeops@example.net
Date: 2026-10-04T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Control-plane / Data-plane synthesis + handoff checkpoints for private VPC

Thanks Mina — review comments from ACME infra team below.

Quick clarifications: 
- Control-plane FQDN: we will expose cp-api.acme.internal (private RFC1918) reachable over the management VPC peering. Confirm Redwood needs a public resolver entry for health-check callbacks or if an internal CNAME is sufficient.
- Egress allowlist: list includes telemetry.redwood.com, s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com; can you provide CIDR ranges for Redwood metrics collectors? Our security team requests stable IP ranges for firewall rules.
- Fallback model: ACME wants the fallback to be explicitly circuit-broken and labeled in metrics so we can track any customer-visible regressions.

Also — on certs: ACME uses Vault Enterprise with a KMS-backed auto-rotating CA. We prefer Redwood to integrate mTLS using certs signed by our CA; will Redwood accept ACME CAs for the control-plane TLS handshake, or do we need to route via Redwood's intermediate?

We’ll mark the handoff_checklist and update rows 5 and 7 with our owner assignments and return by EOD tomorrow.

— Daniel (ACME NetOps)
Daniel R. Lee
Director, Network Operations — ACME Networks
netops@acme.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, netops@acme.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, edgeops@example.net
Date: 2026-10-04T13:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Control-plane / Data-plane synthesis + handoff checkpoints for private VPC

Daniel — good questions. Quick takes from the Redwood ops side: 

- Resolver/health: we do not require a public resolver for the control-plane health callbacks. An internal CNAME that resolves inside the management VPC and across the peering is sufficient. We will run our probes from the management VPC IPs documented in the Drive link — I'll add the collector IPs to the checklist (temporary ranges for staging; final ranges will be published before cutover).

- CIDR for metrics collectors (staging): 10.11.20.0/24 (will expand for prod). We will include these in the handoff_checklist_v2.xlsx. For prod, collectors will come from your agreed regional pool or Redwood-managed egress pool depending on the tenancy model you choose.

- CA integration: Redwood supports customer-supplied CAs for mTLS. For control-plane -> runtime, we need either: (a) ACME's intermediate signed certs that chain to a root we trust, or (b) a short-lived cross-signed cert that Redwood rotates. Option (a) is preferred to avoid extra rotation steps; we’ll need the CA bundle and signing policy.

- Fallback telemetry: we will emit a boolean tag fallback.active and fallback.variant on all span points; Jordan will confirm the metric names and ensure the canary dashboards are configured.

Next step: Jordan, can you put a one-page summary of the runtime ACLs and the exact metric names onto the Drive doc by 15:00 so ACME can validate?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, netops@acme.com
Cc: edgeops@example.net
Date: 2026-10-04T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Control-plane / Data-plane synthesis + handoff checkpoints for private VPC

ACME / Mina / Kim — updating the Drive with the requested artifacts 

Quoted for context: 
> - Fallback telemetry: we will emit a boolean tag fallback.active and fallback.variant on all span points; Jordan will confirm the metric names and ensure the canary dashboards are configured.
> 
> - Egress allowlist: list includes telemetry.redwood.com, s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com; can you provide CIDR ranges for Redwood metrics collectors?

Summary of what I uploaded (Drive link + attached files): 
1) runtime-acls-summary.txt — ports and CIDRs for runtime -> control-plane, runtime -> telemetry collectors, and allowed service endpoints. (Key note: runtime nodes only initiate outbound to TLS endpoints on 443; no SSH hooks.)
2) metrics-namespaces.md — names and tags: "redwood.runtime.fallback.active", "redwood.runtime.fallback.variant", and "redwood.runtime.heartbeat.missed_count". These are mirrored in the canary dashboards we configured in staging.
3) handoff_checklist_v2.xlsx (updated) — marked rows for ACME owner: Network ACLs (row 5), Edge firewall (row 7).

Attachments (again): topology_sketch_v3.png, handoff_checklist_v2.xlsx, runbook_deltas.txt

Runbook/Checkpoints I am calling out explicitly for preflight: 
- CP auth sanity: ACME CA bundle present + test mTLS handshake from staging runtime.
- KV cache routing: confirm that KV cache traffic is pinned to tenant-subnet and not traversing public peering.
- Observability: fallback flag visible in the canary dashboard for at least 10 consecutive minute windows during fault injection.
- Egress proofing: telemetry endpoint accepts staging IPs; no DNS rebinding observed.

If ACME signs off on those items I will open the cutover window in our deployment system and schedule a 60-minute dry-run on the staging slice. If any of the above are NO-GO we will push the cutover until fixes are in.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
